headline: Retrieval grounding checks biomedical LLM outputs against external knowledge sources
label: Retrieval Grounded Biomedical Llms
summary: Recent preprints and publications apply retrieval over curated databases and literature to make LLM answers verifiable in genomics and metadata work.
synthesis: The shared thread is grounding LLM output in external, checkable references rather than parametric knowledge alone. BTE-RAG retrieves from a federated API of over sixty biomedical knowledge sources and improves performance on biomedical benchmarks. RAGulate uses CollecTRI and PubMed evidence to assess transcription factor-target regulatory predictions in context. ChatMDV combines RAG with an LLM to generate reproducible Python visualisations from queries, tested on three scRNA-seq datasets. A FAIRness study pairs GPT-4 with CEDAR metadata templates, raising average dataset retrieval recall from 17.65% to 62.87%. A DGIdb Model Context Protocol server lets LLMs query the drug-gene interaction database directly for druggable genome questions. What is new is treating knowledge bases, literature indices, and metadata schemas as verifiable references against which LLM output is checked. Grounding is the common element, while retrieval architectures and target tasks differ across items.
